name: Soft landing
description: Ions for surface science must land gently, or they would smash the surface: they may arrive with at most a quarter of their launch energy. The two electrodes at the target already brake them; add charges so that they land slowly, on the target, without turning back.

reality.represents: Soft landing: slowing ions gently onto a surface

remarks.line: A potential hill takes the energy
remarks.detail: An ion arrives with its launch energy less q times the potential it climbed: the braking electrodes take the energy back without stopping it short.
Real soft-landing setups slow the ions with electrodes biased close to the ions' energy, landing them at a few eV per charge so that fragile molecules survive; point charges brake them here.
The target is a detector: what the ion does on arrival (sticking, breaking apart, sputtering) is not modelled.

Everything is symmetric about the plane z = 0, so the particle never leaves it. A real beam also has a width across the plane, where the same fields act differently (focusing in the plane can defocus across it).
